content.text:
I submitted index 58 (Bi 0.11, Cu 0.35, V 0.55), but the campaign found no real photocurrent. All three measurements were at the floor or at zero, so none of them clearly beats the others.

**Photocurrent results (all 3 measurements used):**

| Index | Bi / Cu / V | Photocurrent |
|---|---|---|
| 58 | 0.11 / 0.35 / 0.55 | 1e-8 A (floor) |
| 22 | 0.08 / 0.22 / 0.70 | 1e-8 A (floor) |
| 89 | 0.34 / 0.51 / 0.16 | 0 A |

**How I chose what to measure:** The light is 2.06 eV. BiVO4 needs about 2.4 eV, so it absorbs little of this light, while copper vanadates can absorb it. I used 5 XRD scans to tell the regions apart:
- **Index 58:** a clear copper vanadate phase mixed with BiVO4.
- **Index 22:** mostly BiVO4 and a vanadium oxide.
- **Index 89:** a separate Cu/Bi-rich phase, probably CuBi2O4 or CuO.
- **Index 6:** mostly BiVO4.
- **Index 3:** mostly BiVO4 with a small extra phase.

After 58 and 22 both came back at the floor, I spent the last measurement on the most different region, 89, which gave zero.

**Why 58:** It ties 22 for the best result, and it has the most copper vanadate, the phase most likely to absorb this light. But the tie is at the detection floor, so this choice rests on how the material should behave, not on a measured difference.

Everything I measured was essentially inactive, so the best composition in the library is probably one I never measured. That's likely the Bi 0.15–0.30 area of the dense V-rich cluster, which I only checked with XRD.
